summary.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.
summary.overview: Presales of INR868 crore (up 338% YoY) and collections of INR496 crore (up 54% YoY) led the quarter, while no new projects were launched in Q1 by design. Reported revenue from operations fell to INR217 crore from INR681 crore, EBITDA was negative INR106 crore, and net loss widened to INR234 crore from INR166 crore, as revenue is recognised only on completion and handover. Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.

segments.name: Residential (owned development)
segments.commentary: Presales INR868 crore in Q1; ongoing portfolio of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; OC-received inventory about 98% cumulatively sold. Construction spend INR276 crore, about 56% of collections.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Embassy East Business Park is under excavation and may be held as an annuity asset or sold near completion. Embassy Knowledge Park commercial product is in early planning, with timelines targeted by end-FY27; not included in GDV.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance: INR6,000 crore from owned developments and INR2,000 crore from DM projects, reiterated.
FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crore reiterated; management says it could be bettered, with more clarity by Q3.

FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects, GDV about INR19,400 crore (9 owned, INR13,300 crore; 2 DM, INR6,000-plus crore). Four to launch in Q2 (Embassy One North tower, Embassy Knowledge Park villas and apartments, Juhu DM project); the rest targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.
Management expects a cash-flow inflection around mid-calendar 2027 (April-May) as slab cycles start on Greenshore, Verde and Citadel.
Debt: cost of debt to fall first, with refinancing of the portfolio targeted around March-April 2027; net debt to equity target of 0.3x-0.35x.
Under review: percentage-of-completion accounting, to be assessed over the next couple of quarters.
capex_capacity: Ongoing development of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; Embassy Paradiso and balance towers of Golf City Savroli nearing completion and slated for OC in FY27; Embassy Edge and East Avenue due for completion in FY28.
OC received in Q1 for Embassy One 09 (Gurgaon, Phase 1) and 5 towers at Golf City Savroli.
Embassy Citadel (Mumbai, Worli) has approval for all 81 floors; Leighton appointed as civil contractor; est. INR8,000-9,000 crore of stock to sell over several years.

Beyond 2027: development pipeline of about 20.3 million sq ft, GDV about INR23,470 crore; fully paid land bank of 3,000-plus acres, including 1,400-plus acres at Nashik (MIDC dispute; debonding expected to take 6-9 more months).
Cumulative unsold inventory across launched and under-construction residential and commercial projects: INR13,630 crore.
demand_pricing: Bangalore: about 72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months; management cites this as the cleanest read on demand, with Mumbai's 60% figure skewed by Citadel.
Nearly 60% of inventory launched in FY26 already sold.
Management says Embassy has a pricing premium in Bangalore; Citadel's first tranche priced to build reputation before taking top Mumbai pricing.
Collections-to-presales ratio was about 35% last year; FY27 target implies about 50% (INR3,000 crore vs INR6,000 crore owned presales).
Some Gurgaon landlords have asked about the Indiabulls association; management says the entities are separate and that this is a slow-to-resolve perception issue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Bangalore launch delays (as at Prestige) also affecting Embassy, and can the other 5 Bangalore projects launch within FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 non-launch to choice, not approvals; Embassy One North was pushed to Q2 after the Four Seasons branding was dropped. Knowledge Park villas and apartments are targeted for Q2, and Bangalore projects are targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given EBITDA of negative INR106 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore because no launches occurred in Q1; collections from Q3-Q4 FY26 launches should accelerate from Q2. Cash balance started FY27 at about INR1,165 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR19,400 crore GDV split between H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: The four Q2 launches (North tower, Knowledge Park, Juhu DM, plus Embassy One already launched) are in H1; the remaining projects are targeted for Q3, possibly Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average cost of debt and the cost of the Blackstone debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is about 14%. Blackstone debt accrues at 18%, added to the gross debt rather than paid out; management is in talks to convert the Blackstone portion to equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why the promoter warrant issue if the promoter debt is accruing rather than paid in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it brings no new liquidity; it is a confidence signal, priced at INR111.51 (the earlier pre-merger price), and the Embassy Group debt (growing at over 15%) will be cleared. Warrants will convert within 6 months, versus the 18-month maximum.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Most collections are expected from already-launched projects (Greenshore, Verde, Eden). Launches in Q2 and Q3 are expected to yield 10-20% collected in the quarter; management is confident of the INR3,000 crore.

risks_watch: Bangalore launch timing: Embassy One North and Knowledge Park villas/apartments are targeted for Q2, with the other Bangalore and Gurgaon projects targeted for Q3 and possibly spilling into Q4; any slip shifts collections and presales guidance.

Collections guidance of about INR3,000 crore depends on Greenshore, Verde and Eden milestones; management expects Q2 and Q3 launches to contribute 10-20% collected in-quarter, and Q1 collections were INR496 crore, so the run-rate needs to step up sharply.
Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore in Q1; management expects a positive trend from Q2 and a cash-flow inflection around April-May 2027, so track quarterly operating cash flow.

Cost of debt about 14% with Blackstone debt accruing at 18% and added to gross debt; watch the Blackstone equity conversion talks, the refinancing targeted for around March-April 2027, and net debt to equity against the 0.3x-0.35x target.

Nashik land (1,400-plus acres) faces an MIDC dispute and debonding expected to take 6-9 more months; percentage-of-completion accounting is under review over the next couple of quarters, which could change reported revenue and losses.
key_quotes: Presales for Q1 stood at INR868 crores, which is up 338% year-on-year, while collections more importantly, increased 54% to INR496 crores.

We remain comfortable with our FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crores in presales from the owned developments, INR2,000 crores from the developed managed projects and approximately INR3,000 crores of collections.
So, we are going to see a very robust collection in the next -- from the next quarter onwards.
And I really feel that the inflection point in this company will really happen at some point mid of next calendar year.
So, I think legally, it will go slowly.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on presales, demand and collections guidance, but cautious and deflective on reported losses, Bangalore launch timing and Nashik, repeatedly pointing to future cash inflection. Answers on cash flow and the warrant issue were more defensive, with the CFO stressing it brings no new liquidity.
